subject: JSON handshake & function-calling discovery — PayFlux / Redwood recap
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex@payflux.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-28T15:02:00Z
Subject: JSON handshake & function-calling discovery — PayFlux / Redwood recap

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call.

Attendees: Alex Kim (PayFlux), Nisha Rana (PayFlux), Camila Reyes (Redwood), Ben Carter (Redwood), Aditya Rao (Redwood)

Key pain points (as discussed):
- Downstream reconciliation pipeline cannot tolerate malformed or variant outputs; current LLM outputs are inconsistent across versions and prompts.
- They need to reliably extract structured actions (e.g., {"action":"create_charge", "amount":...}) for orchestration into their Node microservices.
- High volume of small transactions — requirement for deterministic formatting and idempotent action identifiers to avoid double charges.
- Compliance constraints: audit logs, SSO, and SOC2 scope for production data.

Current stack notes:
- PayFlux: Node services + Kafka for events, PostgreSQL for ledger, Stripe for settlement; internal orchestration layer that expects strictly typed JSON payloads.
- Integrations: REST endpoints and a small adapter that validates schema before persisting.

Success criteria (customer-defined):
1) >99% JSON schema validity against provided schema for the evaluation prompt set.
2) Deterministic field presence and top-level "action" normalization (allowed list: create_charge, refund, void, update_metadata).
3) Action-level idempotency key included when appropriate.
4) 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency < 200ms for single-request path during POC target load.
5) Observability: per-request cost and token breakdown in the console; audit log export for each PII-scoped request.

What we (Redwood) will deliver for the POC:
- A 2-week technical eval with a dedicated test model + quantization profile tuned to their load.
- Shared prompt and schema file (attached: schema_v1.json and payflux_sample_promptset.csv).
- A minimal adapter template and a suggested validation harness (redwood_poc_plan.pdf).

Proposed next steps & timeline:
- PayFlux to confirm technical acceptance criteria and any additional fields to lock in schema (requested by 2026-03-31).
- Redwood to schedule a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive with Nisha (engineer) and our runtime team (propose Fri Apr 2 10:00am PT).
- Execute a short SOW/NDA if required; Redwood will surface a standard POC SOW draft.

Questions for you before the deep-dive:
- Do you need EU-only residency for this POC data or is US-hosted acceptable for now?
- Any additional telemetry points you need us to emit for your reconciliation service?

Thanks — attaching the POC plan and schema. I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep-dive.

—
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

A few clarifications / asks from our side:

- SOC2 is a hard requirement for production; for the POC we can run on US-hosted infra but will need to validate the audit logs and retention policies.
- Our legal team will want a short POC agreement outlining data usage and deletion policy; can your team share a template?
- We would like the evaluation to include a short negative prompt set (cases where model should refuse) — we will share examples.

Proposed timeline looks good — Nisha: are you available Apr 2 morning PT?
